reason: The text contains numerous regular human characters who demonstrate clear agency. These include: the messengers and servants who report the king's inquiries (they are sent, return, and speak); the captains of fifty who carry out military orders with various outcomes; Elisha, who follows Elijah and makes deliberate choices throughout (refusing to stay behind, requesting a double portion of Elijah's spirit); the prophets/sons of the prophets from Bethel and Jericho who speak with Elisha and conduct a search; the men of the city who approach Elisha with their water problem; and the young men who mock Elisha on the road. All these characters perform actions, make decisions, deliver messages, and affect the narrative through their choices and behaviors, rather than merely serving as backdrop to divine or prophetic action.
